core.role: Shared tasks, models, data, evaluation, metrics, and baseline CLIs.

length_generalisation.role: Pointer pipelines, sparse and hard attention, compiled routing, and length MAML.

shortcut_learning.role: Learned backward rules, selectors, collapse diagnostics, and shortcut MAML.

transfer.role: Compiled-circuit transfer to downstream puzzles and language modelling.

experiments.question: How do direct Transformer and LSTM sorting baselines change outside the length-2-to-20 training range?
experiments.evaluation_domain: Length sweeps recorded in the committed metrics and plots.
experiments.summary: Useful original baselines, retained as historical context rather than a current headline result.

experiments.question: Do textual quicksort traces or executor-assisted traces make list sorting generalise in length?
experiments.training_domain: Online sorting traces generated from lists of length 2-20.
experiments.evaluation_domain: Longer list lengths recorded in committed metrics.
experiments.summary: Representation studies motivated the smaller pointer diagnostics. They are no longer the preferred experimental interface.

experiments.question: Which positional-attention pattern lets a causal Transformer retrieve the value after a pointer at unseen positions?
experiments.summary: Alternating RoPE/NoPE was much stronger than all-RoPE or all-NoPE in one controlled seed; rotating values failed.

experiments.question: Can pointer retrieval and comparison be learned as an autoregressive sequence of modular position operations?
experiments.training_domain: Pipeline stages trained on list lengths 2-20.
experiments.summary: The staged curriculum isolates routing operations and gives strong single-seed transfer, but later stages remain less stable and are not a general sorting solution.

experiments.question: Does an exactly compiled routing circuit transfer better than random initialization?
experiments.training_domain: Four downstream tasks at lengths 2-20, three matched seeds.
experiments.summary: Compiled-prefix transfer helps tasks that reuse locate-and-retrieve operations, but not the unrelated Dyck-2 task.

experiments.question: Do compiled routing blocks improve byte language modelling or context-length extrapolation?
experiments.training_domain: Three paired seeds, 5,000 updates, 256-byte contexts from a fixed Pile slice.
experiments.summary: Random initialization beats trainable and frozen compiled-middle variants in-domain and at every longer tested context.

experiments.question: Can forward-only EGGROLL learn a minimal top-1 attention routing algorithm that extrapolates in length?
experiments.training_domain: Performance curriculum from length 2 to 20, then top-k and head-pruning curricula.
experiments.summary: One seed recovered strong long-length accuracy after pruning to one deterministic top-1 head per layer.

experiments.question: Which attention and output-trace choices support pointer retrieval and local comparison beyond the training lengths?
experiments.training_domain: Pointer-next and pointer-comparison lists of length 2-20, one seed per ablation.
experiments.evaluation_domain: Recurring evaluations through length 2,000 and selected final evaluations at 5,000.
experiments.summary: Dense softmax and fixed scaling are sufficient for pointer-next. On matched 20,000-step autoregressive traces, entmax reached 100% exact accuracy through sampled length 5,000 with and without a final KEEP/SWAP target; softmax reached 10.9% and 46.9%, respectively.

experiments.question: Can an evolved attention-gradient router selected at length 50 improve length-400 generalisation?
experiments.evaluation_domain: Fixed ranking and acceptance sets at length 50; length 400 reporting-only.
experiments.summary: No stable length-400 advantage was established; optimization cost, collapse, and weak ranking-to-heldout transfer remain confounded.

experiments.question: Can differentiating through short-task updates improve longer-length pointer solutions?
experiments.training_domain: Persistent pointer-next models trained at lengths 2-20 with one-step or horizon-24 meta updates.
experiments.evaluation_domain: Meta objectives around length 50 and reporting at length 400.
experiments.summary: Several variants learned the length-50 objective but did not provide a stable length-400 advantage; horizon-24 routing collapsed toward broad suppression.

experiments.question: Can scarce fixed clean fitness data evolve a backward rule that learns the intended pointer function from unlimited shortcut-containing training data?
experiments.training_domain: Random-position shortcut examples resampled online; forward models reset across evolutionary trajectories.
experiments.evaluation_domain: A fixed clean fitness set for evolution and fresh masked/incorrect-hint sets for reporting.
experiments.summary: A selected backward rule transfers across fresh forward-model trajectories on the same shortcut task and strongly outperforms ordinary backpropagation.

experiments.question: Can evolution repair the later trajectory regions where an initially robust shortcut rule collapses?
experiments.training_domain: Saved collapse windows and on-policy trajectories from the random-position shortcut task.
experiments.evaluation_domain: Seed-disjoint windows plus complete held-out trajectories.
experiments.summary: Candidates improved selected windows but did not pass the complete on-policy acceptance gate; state-conditioned follow-ups were rejected.

experiments.question: Is modifying backward credit on attention scores sufficient in principle to prevent the explicit shortcut?
experiments.training_domain: Shortcut-containing data with known leak-token locations.
experiments.evaluation_domain: Fixed and fresh clean, masked-hint, incorrect-hint, and correct-hint examples.
experiments.summary: Oracle attention-score reversal solves both suffix and random-position variants; broader QKV or complete-attention reversal does not.

experiments.question: Can a learned binary token policy discover where attention-score gradients should be reversed?
experiments.training_domain: Group-reward evolutionary or GRPO-style training on shortcut examples.
experiments.summary: The learned selector did not improve held-out clean accuracy despite the successful oracle mechanism.

experiments.question: Can a persistent attention-gradient router be meta-learned through short shortcut-training trajectories?
experiments.training_domain: Random-position shortcut examples with persistent forward model and router.
experiments.evaluation_domain: Masked and incorrect-hint held-out data after one-, eight-, or 24-step lookahead.
experiments.summary: Longer lookahead produced a strong single-seed shortcut result, but the method was less effective and less robust than the evolutionary rule.
